mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across historical data without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that typically precedes economic slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown in both consumer and business sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced growth expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as higher interest rates compress equity valuations and slow economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.2% signals rising inflation that may prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher interest rates and reduced real earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.2%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days as elevated joblessness signals weak consumer demand and corporate profit pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5% signals a manufacturing contraction that typically precedes economic slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when INDPRO monthly change < -0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
